text: Known issue, not fixed: when the Voice PE firmware reopens the ES7210 mic for a session, it does not drop the ~100 ms codec startup transient (the wake-word path drops it via WARMUP_DISCARD_MS in trigger.c). The transient reaches the server VAD and STT. Fix belongs in the firmware. Trimming the first 100 ms on the server was rejected because it would cut real speech when there is no transient (2026-11-08).

Rejected: keeping a warm/pooled ElevenLabs realtime STT socket between runs to remove dial latency after the wake word. ElevenLabs closes idle realtime sessions, so it needs keepalive and reconnect logic. Chosen instead: dial per run in a background worker and buffer audio until the socket opens (2026-11-08).

Rejected (2026-11): moving runPipelineResponse into a goroutine so the device read loop stays free during the webhook and TTS. The ping concern does not apply, because the server sends pings from its own goroutine and the amoledesp32 client cancels a run itself after 60 s with no events. The real failure (the read deadline expiring during a long run) was fixed by setting the deadline before each read. Revisit only if cancel handling during the webhook wait becomes necessary.

Until 2026-11-23 the server fed Silero bare 512-sample windows without the 64-sample context, so all scores were too low. speechStartThreshold, speechContinueThreshold, speechStartFramesRequired, silenceFramesRequired, preSpeechTimeout and audioCaptureWindow were all tuned against those wrong scores and were deliberately left unchanged when the context was fixed. Intent: collect the peak values from the end-of-speech and capture-window log lines over a few days of real sessions, including some with a television on, then decide the thresholds (they will probably go up). Television noise with context was never measured; the accepted risk is that sessions with a television on run to the 15 s capture cap. Separate open decision: the +12 dB session gain in the Stavvy device firmware was added to compensate for low scores and may be unnecessary now.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>
